tools_found.signal_summary: Cisco rolled out GitHub Copilot at scale to its developer workforce (reported ~6,000 developers in one business group) with dedicated training, and Cisco engineers/researchers published a peer study evaluating Copilot on real proprietary Cisco codebases. Cisco IT publicly reports AI-first engineering with Copilot driving large output gains.

evidence.claim: GitHub's official rollout guidance cites Cisco rolling out Copilot to ~6,000 developers in a business group and partnering with GitHub Premium Support for training sessions on prompting and best practices.
evidence.quote: When Cisco rolled out Copilot to their 6,000 developers in their business group, they were eager and excited, but had plenty of questions.

evidence.claim: A peer-reviewed/arXiv study titled 'Transforming Software Development: Evaluating the Efficiency and Challenges of GitHub Copilot in Real-World Projects' was conducted at Cisco with 26 engineers on large proprietary codebases, identifying 15 dev tasks and finding up to 50% time saved on documentation/autocomplete and 30-40% on repetitive coding, projecting 33-36% overall time reduction.
evidence.quote: explores the impact of GitHub Copilot within a real-world, cloud-first software development environment at Cisco

evidence.claim: Cisco IT publicly states AI-first engineering with tools like GitHub Copilot shows a 3X increase in output, shifting from human coding to human review, with 30-50% productivity gains across IT functions (projected 36% overall).
evidence.quote: AI-first engineering with tools like GitHub Copilot shows a 3X increase in output, shifting from human coding to human review.

evidence.claim: A Webex Developers blog describes a Cisco Webex Engineering Technical Leader using Microsoft/GitHub Copilot in VS Code (plus an in-house ChatGPT) to evaluate, explain, and document Python sample scripts.

tools_found.tool_name: Copilot agent mode / agentic coding agents (general)
tools_found.signal_summary: A Cisco Live EMEA 2026 conference talk by a Cisco CX Engineering Principal Engineer covers the developer journey from Copilot (assistant) to agent (agentic coding), indicating Cisco engineers are moving toward agentic developer tooling.

evidence.claim: Cisco Live EMEA 2026 session AI-2957 'From Copilot to Agent: A Developer's Journey into AI-Powered Engineering' was presented by John Groetzinger, Principal Engineer in Cisco CX Engineering (Generative AI and Network Security).
evidence.quote: From Copilot to Agent: A Developer's Journey into AI-Powered Engineering

tools_found.signal_summary: A GitHub organization named 'ciscoittech' hosts an open-source 'claude-agent-framework' for orchestrating parallel Claude Code agents, claiming production-derived patterns. Cisco affiliation of the org is not independently confirmed, so this is a weak/ambiguous signal.

evidence.claim: GitHub org 'ciscoittech' publishes 'claude-agent-framework', a framework for building multi-agent development systems with Claude Code (claims ~97% context reduction and 3-6x faster execution via parallel agents, 'built from real-world patterns used in production').
evidence.quote: Complete framework for building intelligent multi-agent development systems with Claude Code.

tools_found.tool_name: JARVIS (Cisco Outshift internal AI Platform Engineer)
tools_found.signal_summary: JARVIS is a Cisco-built (Outshift) internal multi-agent platform-engineering assistant (LangGraph/LangSmith) used by Cisco engineers to automate developer requests, CI/CD pipeline setup, and operational tasks. This is Cisco-built internal automation rather than a third-party coding agent, but it is Cisco engineers using agentic AI in their dev workflow.

evidence.claim: Cisco Outshift's JARVIS is a multi-agent system (15+ sub-agents, 40 tool integrations) surfaced into Jira, Backstage, Webex, and CLI; the team reports a 10x productivity boost, CI/CD pipeline setup cut from 5-7 days to under an hour, and up to 70% time saved on repetitive ops.
evidence.quote: How Outshift by Cisco achieved a 10x productivity boost with their Agentic AI Platform Engineer

evidence.claim: Cisco's own Outshift blog describes JARVIS as an Iron Man-inspired agent transforming platform engineering at Outshift.

notes: Searches run (~14): Claude Code + Cisco dogfooding; GitHub Copilot + Cisco adoption; Cursor + Cisco; Copilot 6000 developers case study; Cisco engineering blog internal AI assistant; Jeetu Patel/earnings AI coding; Amazon Q/Gemini CLI/Windsurf/Devin + Cisco; Cisco 'AI-first engineering' 3X; Cisco software-engineer job postings naming tools; Outshift/JARVIS; Cisco Security 'Transforming Software Development' Copilot study; Webex + Copilot Microsoft customer story; Cisco Live talks; Cisco + Claude enterprise; agent mode + Cisco internal; ciscoittech org verification. STRONGEST/most credible: GitHub Copilot — corroborated by GitHub's own rollout guidance (6,000 devs), an arXiv study at Cisco (26 engineers, real proprietary code), and Cisco IT's blog (3X output). CAVEATS: (1) Several primary URLs (Cisco blogs, arXiv, Webex dev blog, Cisco Live PDF, GitHub resources) returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; claims rest on search-result snippets of those REAL URLs, not full-text fetch. (2) The 'ciscoittech' GitHub org's Cisco affiliation is NOT independently confirmed — could be a personal/unofficial handle borrowing the name; treat Claude Code signal as weak. (3) JARVIS and Cisco's internal AI Assistant (156k daily interactions, 100k users) are Cisco-BUILT products/automation, not third-party coding agents — included as context but distinguished from third-party coding-agent dogfooding. (4) No evidence found for Cisco engineers using Amazon Q Developer, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, OpenAI Codex/Operator, Devin, Windsurf, or Cowork as developer tools; those searches returned only generic listicles/comparisons. No direct exec/earnings quote tying Cisco coding-agent use to a named executive was found.
